headline: High-risk shared-workspace coding agent can overwrite or mislead a read-only orchestrator; prompt-injection and leakage are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cline can ingest workspace files, browser screenshots, and MCP outputs, so malicious content could influence it. Dagster is read-only and has no file or MCP surfaces, so the interaction is one-way and requires manual bridging or shared files. The pathway exists, but the blast radius is limited by Dagster's lack of direct input channels.
conditions: IF the operator copies untrusted text from Cline-managed files into Dagster task definitions, injection becomes reachable.
IF Dagster is extended with a file-ingest step that consumes Cline output, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Keep Dagster inputs separate from Cline workspace files.
Review any copied prompts or task specs before pasting.
Disable MCP servers that expose untrusted content to Cline.
Use a dedicated staging folder for artifacts from Cline.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cline touches source code and browser screenshots and can read/write the workspace, while Dagster exposes no filesystem or network surfaces in this profile. That makes leakage possible mainly through shared workspace files or copied outputs, not through a direct automatic channel. The blast radius is limited because Dagster itself is not shown to exfiltrate data.
conditions: IF sensitive source code is stored in the shared workspace and then opened by Dagster-side tooling, leakage becomes possible.
IF the operator exports Cline outputs into Dagster logs or metadata, those contents may persist.
mitigations: Store secrets outside the shared workspace.
Redact screenshots before moving them between tools.
Keep Dagster metadata free of raw Cline transcripts.
Use separate OS users or directories for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs and secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cline has broad filesystem write, shell, and git mutation in a per-workspace session, and shared state with other instances is explicitly via filesystem. Dagster has no write or shell capability here, so direct conflict is asymmetric, but Cline can still race with Dagster-managed files or artifacts in the same workspace. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration boundary pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Dagster writes artifacts into the same directory Cline edits, file clobbering can occur.
IF Cline and Dagster both mutate git-tracked files without locking, conflicts can corrupt state.
mitigations: Assign separate directories for Dagster outputs and Cline edits.
Pause Cline before Dagster writes shared artifacts.
Use git locks or a single writer policy.
Check in generated files only after review.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cline can generate code, browser-derived facts, and file edits, and Dagster commonly orchestrates downstream work; even though Dagster's runnable/action surfaces are not exposed here, the pair still creates a plausible path where Cline output is treated as authoritative. Because Dagster's execution behavior is not documented in this profile, uncertainty escalates to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dagster consumes Cline-produced files as pipeline inputs without validation, errors can cascade.
IF Cline's browser-derived claims are promoted into Dagster metadata or alerts, downstream actions may be wrong.
mitigations: Require validation before Dagster consumes Cline outputs.
Separate generated facts from executable pipeline config.
Add human review for any Cline-authored DAG changes.
Log source provenance on all imported artifacts.
requires-engineering: add schema checks and approval gates.

E_compliance.rationale: Cline handles model-provider API keys and browser screenshots, while Dagster's profile shows no secrets, no network egress, and no data classes touched. There is no direct evidence of a residency or certification mismatch, so compliance risk is limited to accidental handling of sensitive workspace data by Cline alone. Dagster is not cited for a specific violation because its profile lacks such data flows.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workspace and then processed by Cline, compliance obligations may apply.
IF Dagster is configured to store Cline outputs in a regulated repository, retention policy mismatches can arise.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace.
Review retention settings for any logs or artifacts.
Avoid copying screenshots containing personal data.
Document which system is the system of record.
requires-engineering: add policy-based data classification controls.
